Senses.Explanation: The records define straight mind against bends, twists, crookedness, and falseness: ‘straight mind means without bends or twists.’ Literally, a straight or straightforward mind. The term occurs 163 times in 89 allowed texts. The corpus supplies two compact definitions: 'straight mind means without bends or twists' (直心者，無委曲故), and 'straight mind is the site of the Way because it has no falseness' (直心是道場，無虛假故). The Platform Record repeats 'straight mind is the site; straight mind is the clean land' (直心是道場，straight mind is the clean land, ‘straight mind is the site; straight mind is the clean land’), then contrasts inwardly acting crookedly while verbally speaking straight with actually carrying out straight mind. Its positive clause is 'only carry out straight mind; regarding all things, have no grasping' (但行直心，於一切法上，無有執著). Another address expands the pattern into four coordinated expressions: 'straight mind is the site; straight speech is the subtle teaching; straight conduct is subtle conduct; straight verification is the subtle result' (直心是道場，直說是妙法，直行是妙行，直證是妙果). The common collocation 'straight mind and straight conduct' (直心直行) occurs 22 times in 16 texts. One record describes it by the absence of self-versus-other, right-versus-wrong, falseness, and crookedness; another uses 'straight mind, straight conduct, original color, original share' (直心直行，本色本分) to characterize a named Chan figure's meetings with people.
Senses.Note: The English follows the graph meaning 'straight' (直) and the texts' own oppositions: straight versus crooked (直／曲), genuine versus false (genuine / false), and straight conduct versus flattering crookedness (諂曲). The direct definition 'without bends or twists' occurs once, while the site-of-the-Way formula occurs across multiple independent records. No master-specific sense is warranted.

Occurrences.AttributionNote: Source text (南宗頓教最上大乘摩訶般若波羅蜜經六祖惠能大師於韶州大梵寺施法壇經). Platform Record. Huineng contrasts speaking straight while acting crookedly with carrying out straight mind, then says to have no grasping regarding anything.

Occurrences.Kwic: 所謂直心是道場，直說是妙法，直行是妙行，直證是妙果。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Recorded Sayings of Chan Master Yinyuan (隱元禪師語錄), Yinyuan Longqi's Huangbo Mountain record. In a release-of-retreat address, Yinyuan Longqi says that direct mind is the site of the Way, direct speech the wondrous teaching, direct action the wondrous conduct, and direct realization the wondrous fruit.

Occurrences.Kwic: 所云直心是道場，無虛假故。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Recorded Sayings of Chan Master Yingning Jing (攖寧靜禪師語錄), in Yingning Jing's continued reply. The formula introduced by '(所云)' quotes Vimalakirti's answer to the youth Light Adornment: Vimalakirti is the exact quoted speaker who says that straight mind is the site of awakening because it has no falseness. An independent corpus witness preserves the full named dialogue; Yunmen Wenyan is neither the source nor the section's Yunmen addressee.
